notes: Planning-workflow evals. Each run gets a disposable repo fixture and an isolated FORGE_DATA_DIR with a pre-seeded board (custom statuses, one existing overlapping issue) so duplicates, preserved settings and unintended runs are observable. Baseline = shipped skill.

evals.name: small-api-feature
evals.prompt: We need a DELETE /notes/:id endpoint in this notes API. Plan it into the 'Notes API' board so someone can pick it up later — don't build it yet. Work only in the current directory; don't push or clone anything.
assertions: Reads the repository (server/route code or tests) before writing issues
Reuses the existing 'Notes API' board (no project_create)
Does not create an issue duplicating the existing 'Add request logging' issue
Each new issue body contains checkable acceptance criteria
Each new issue states how to verify it (tests/commands)
States an explicit decision on API behaviour for a missing id (e.g. 404) or asks one focused question about it
Does not call project_run and does not modify repository files
Preserves the board's existing statuses, priorities and attachments
Every new leaf (non-umbrella) issue body contains its own verify step naming a concrete command or check (judge from issues_full.json)
Identifies that len(notes)+1 id allocation breaks once deletes exist and orders the fix before the endpoint via set_blocked_by

evals.name: multi-module-change
evals.prompt: Add a 'priority' field to tasks across the whole stack here — the storage schema, the core library and the CLI (existing stored tasks must keep working). Break this into tickets on the 'Taskr' board with the right dependencies. I approve the plan in advance, just get it on the board. Work only in the current directory; don't push or clone anything.
assertions: Reads the modules involved (storage, core, cli) before planning
Creates more than one issue, each scoped to an independently reviewable change
Uses set_blocked_by for ordering between dependent issues (not only sub-issue nesting)
Blockers point in the correct direction (schema/storage before core, core before CLI)
Makes an explicit data-migration / backwards-compatibility decision for existing stored tasks
Mentions a rollback or reversibility approach for the schema change
Does not call project_run despite the plan being approved, and does not edit repository files
Preserves the board's existing statuses, priorities and attachments
Every new leaf issue body contains its own acceptance criteria and a concrete verify command (judge from issues_full.json)
Flags the overlap/interaction with the existing 'Add a `done` command to the CLI' issue instead of ignoring it

evals.name: ambiguous-requirement
evals.prompt: make the notes api faster and more scalable, put a plan on the Notes API board
assertions: Inspects the code to ground what 'faster' could mean (e.g. storage, handlers) before planning
Either asks at most one consolidated message of questions, or proceeds with explicitly stated assumptions
Does not ask about things answerable from the repository
Any issues created have measurable acceptance criteria (a number or a concrete check), not 'make it faster'
Does not create a new board and does not duplicate existing issues
Does not call project_run and does not modify repository files
Flags any API-compatibility impact (e.g. changed GET /notes response) as a decision or assumption rather than silently planning a breaking change
Includes a baseline/before-and-after measurement step so 'faster' is proven
Risky concurrency work (threaded server) is blocked until the store is safe for concurrent access, or not planned
